title: task_lifecycle_duplicate_identity guidance names only the partial-git-add cause, not the completed-then-restored shape
description:
Follow-up to QCLI-261 (Done), which made the duplicate-identity error name every colliding path and give rm/git-rm recovery. Found by glyph-cli and relayed by opum-agent (OPAG-846); glyph fixed its own side in opum-ai/glyph-cli#9.

WHAT IS NEW: the current hint names one cause -- "usually a partial `git add` that staged a move's addition but not its deletion" -- while a second, plausibly more common cause produces the identical state and needs a different emphasis in recovery.

MEASURED HERE against the installed 0.11.0 and the dev-built 0.12.0 binary (identical hint text on both, exit 5): in a scratch workspace, `quest task complete <id>` on a branch yields an uncommitted, worktree-only move -- ` D .quest/tasks/<id>.json` plus untracked `?? .quest/completed/<id>.json`. Any operation that then discards that tracked deletion while leaving the untracked addition restored the tasks/ copy BESIDE the completed/ copy: reproduced with `git switch -f <branch>`, `git reset --hard`, and `git restore --worktree -- .quest`. Every quest command then fails closed (conflict, exit 5; `quest doctor` exits 5 too). A partial git add is NOT present in this shape, so the single cause named in the hint misleads.

Two plain-switch outcomes, measured in the same sweep and recorded because they narrow the shape rather than match the relay: a PLAIN `git switch` does NOT produce the duplicate -- it carries the unstaged deletion, leaving a consistent tree with the record found under completed/. And when the move was COMMITTED before the switch, the switch back restores tasks/<id>.json and removes completed/<id>.json, silently reverting the completion with no error at all. Both are silent; only the force/restore variants produce the duplicate.

WHY THE RECOVERY DIFFERS: for the branch-switch shape the completed/ copy is the true current state, so the fix is to remove the STALE tasks/ copy and then COMMIT the move -- both the deletion and the addition. Removing the stale copy without landing the move leaves the addition untracked, so the next restoring operation can recreate the duplicate.

OPTIONAL (requester-flagged, no design decided): the error or `quest doctor` could detect which shape it is -- in the stale-copy case tasks/<id>.json is tracked at HEAD while completed/<id>.json is untracked or newly added -- and say so instead of a generic compare-them-yourself.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The duplicate-identity guidance names the second cause: a lifecycle move made on one branch and left uncommitted, then an operation that discards the tracked deletion (`git switch -f`, `git reset --hard`, `git restore/checkout of .quest`) while the untracked completed/ copy survives.

For that cause the guidance gives the matching recovery: remove the stale tasks/<id>.json AND land the move (commit the deletion and the addition), because removing the stale copy alone leaves the next restoring operation free to recreate the duplicate.

Optional (requester-flagged, no design decided): a caller can distinguish the two shapes -- the stale-copy shape has tasks/<id>.json tracked at HEAD while completed/<id>.json is untracked or newly added -- and the error or `quest doctor` reports which shape it found; if not pursued, the record says why the distinction is not drawn.

plan: 1. Rewrite the duplicate-identity hint in src/cli/main.ts to name cause (2) - a lifecycle move left uncommitted, then an operation that discards the tracked deletion - and the matching recovery: remove the stale tasks/ copy AND land the move by committing both sides.

2. Add test/qcli424-duplicate-identity-guidance.test.ts: build the duplicate via git reset --hard, assert the hint text from the CLI, execute the recovery and assert the duplicate stays gone after a further reset, and pin the control that a plain switch does not duplicate.
3. AC3 (optional shape detection) not pursued: it needs git-state inspection in a path that never runs git; record the reason and route the question to opum-agent.
4. bun run check under pinned 1.4.2; branch, PR, required checks, merge.
implementationNotes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-30 (session 8e31abf1). The duplicate-identity hint in src/cli/main.ts now names both causes and matches each with its recovery. Cause (1) is QCLI-261's, retained: a partial `git add` that staged a move's addition but not its deletion. Cause (2), new: a lifecycle move (complete/archive) made on a branch and left uncommitted, then an operation that discards the tracked deletion (`git switch -f`, `git reset --hard`, `git restore`/`git checkout` of .quest) while the untracked completed/ copy survives. For cause (2) the hint states the completed/ copy is the true current state, that removing the stale tasks/<id>.json is only half the recovery, and that the move must be landed as well -- commit the deletion and the addition -- because removing the stale copy alone leaves the next restoring operation free to recreate the duplicate.

VERIFIED. New test/qcli424-duplicate-identity-guidance.test.ts, three CLI-level tests against real scratch workspaces: (1) the guidance text, read from a real conflict envelope after the measured shape is built; (2) the recovery executed -- removing the stale copy alone unblocks the next command, a further `git reset --hard` with the move still unlanded recreates the duplicate (the half-recovery control the hint's second clause is about), and after committing both sides a further reset leaves the tree clean and the record Done; (3) the plain-switch control -- a plain `git switch` carries the uncommitted move without duplicating, so only the DISCARD produces the duplicate. Mutation proof of the guidance test's teeth: reverting the hint to HEAD's text reddens exactly test (1) with tests (2) and (3) green; restored, 3 of 3. Full `bun run check` under pinned bun 1.4.2: 1063 pass, 0 fail, with typecheck, lint, format:check and layer:check clean.

AC3 NOT PURSUED, and this is the reason the distinction is not drawn. It is requester-flagged optional with no design decided, and pursuing it requires deciding three things the task text leaves open: the surface (the conflict error vs `quest doctor`), the reporting channel (hint prose vs an additive `input` field on the conflict envelope, which is a contract-shape choice), and the fallback when git state cannot be read (no repository here, git unavailable). It is NOT blocked on capability: src/adapters/git/local-git.ts readBlob("HEAD", path) already answers tracked-at-HEAD, so the detection itself is a small extension of an adapter that exists. Routed to opum-agent with this evidence rather than decided here (landing report, 2026-09-30).
finalSummary: Rewrote the duplicate-identity hint so both causes are named and each carries its recovery. Cause (2) -- a lifecycle move left uncommitted on a branch, then an operation that discards the tracked deletion (git switch -f, git reset --hard, git restore/checkout of .quest) while the untracked completed/ copy survives -- is now named beside QCLI-261's partial-git-add cause, and for it the hint states that the completed/ copy is the true state: remove the stale tasks/ copy AND land the move by committing both sides, since removing the stale copy alone lets the next restoring operation recreate the duplicate. Verified by three new CLI-level tests (guidance text; the recovery executed, including the half-recovery control; the plain-switch control), a mutation showing the guidance test reddens on exactly the old hint, and the full check (1063 pass, 0 fail). AC3 (optional shape detection) not pursued: feasible via the existing git adapter, but it needs a decision on surface, reporting channel and fallback; reason recorded and the question routed to opum-agent.
